title: Monomorphisation
concept: Monomorphisation compiles generic code into separate concrete versions for each type used — delivering zero runtime overhead.
why: Understanding monomorphisation explains why generics have no performance penalty: they're not runtime-polymorphic, they're compile-time-specialized.
tips: Don't worry about generic performance — monomorphisation makes them as fast as hand-written code
If binary size is critical, consider using trait objects for large numbers of types
The compiler only generates code for types you ACTUALLY use, not all possible types
common_mistakes: Assuming generics have runtime overhead (vtable) — they don't; XIOM uses monomorphisation
Over-using generics for things that don't need to be generic — each type creates more code
Confusing monomorphisation with dynamic dispatch — XIOM generics are always monomorphised
